name: single-commit atomic role-local manifest plus binary publication

atomicity_argument.public_git_semantics: Both path entries were placed in one tree, one commit points to that tree, and the branch ref was moved once to that commit. The publication point is therefore the single ref transition rather than two sequential path mutations.
atomicity_argument.partial_state_before_ref_update: new blobs/tree/commit may exist but are unreachable from branch; useful bundle is not published
atomicity_argument.partial_state_after_ref_update: both tree entries are branch-visible together
atomicity_argument.duplicate_retry_rule: If both target paths expose the recorded manifest and payload blob SHAs, DONE_NOOP. Any mismatch requires a fresh-parent reconstruction; never patch only one member as completion of the same op_id.

transversal_value: One Git Data commit can atomically publish multiple role-local text/binary identities, reducing partial-write recovery complexity while sharing the same fast-forward conflict discipline used for checkpoint state.

quota_and_cost.api_usage: constant-count repository metadata/content operations; no API-as-compute loop

scope_limits: Atomicity is Git commit/ref atomicity for one repository branch, not a distributed transaction with external systems.
Path SHA identity is reliable in this test; connector binary content rendering is not generally byte-faithful.
No large artifact or repository limit claim.
